memory_update.text: Politics should remain modeled as policy-driven budget, procurement, compliance, domestic-content, tariff, sanctions, and regulatory shocks rather than as one investable sector.
Defense subtier suppliers remain the strongest Layer 1 cluster because DoD supply chains can span five to six tiers while visibility often fades beyond tier two.

Qualified aerospace/defense materials, composites, specialty metals, electronics, test systems, and sustainment distributors deserve higher priority than obvious primes when looking for underfollowed politics beneficiaries.
Rare-earth magnet compliance should be tracked separately from rare-earth mining because the policy chokepoint may be qualified non-Chinese feedstock and magnet capacity.
Tariff, customs, sanctions, and country-of-origin compliance software is a second-order Politics lane that needs a separate Layer 1B pass with primary filings and customer evidence.

The current universe is too defense-heavy; next passes should validate non-defense politics nodes including trade compliance, civic/election infrastructure, border and immigration systems, public-sector software, and energy/permitting beneficiaries.
Before Layer 2, every candidate needs refreshed market cap, valuation, revenue exposure, backlog, analyst coverage, short interest, liquidity, and direct procurement/filing evidence.

summary: Merged Layer 1 universe for the Politics theme, modeled as policy-driven budget, procurement, domestic-content, sanctions, tariff, and compliance shocks rather than a single sector trade. The highest Serenity relevance clusters around defense subtier visibility, qualified aerospace/defense materials, sustainment and distribution, rare-earth magnet/feedstock compliance, customs and trade-compliance software, and niche election/government infrastructure. This is an initial research universe, not a buy/sell list. Priority favors names close to mandatory demand, qualification bottlenecks, lower-tier supply constraints, or compliance gates, while preserving reference leaders needed for supply-chain mapping.
